The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=h(x)$ are given above. Find ${p}^{′}(2)$ where $p(x)=f(x)h(x).$

${p}^{′}(2)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The product rule for derivatives gives

$$
{p}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)\cdot h(x)+f(x)\cdot {h}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{p}^{′}(2)={f}^{′}(2)\cdot h(2)+f(2)\cdot {h}^{′}(2).
$$

From the graphs above, we obtain that $f(2)=1$ and $h(2)=-1.$

Additionally,

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (1,3)$ equals $-1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(2)=-1.$

- The slope of $h(x)$ on $x\in (1,3)$ equals $-2.$ So, ${h}^{′}(2)=-2.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(2) & ={f}^{′}(2)\cdot h(2)+f(2)\cdot {h}^{′}(2) \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)+1\cdot (-2) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
